done_when: A thread follow-up starts a turn only when the new batch has a message from an allowed sender, proven by a test where only the root sender is allowed and another person's follow-up gets no reply

findings.body: The new Postgres test improves the earlier unit-only proof, but still does not meet the required end-to-end boundary. It replaces internal sender authorization with a mock at lines 54–56, configures that mock at line 763, and directly calls storage and processGroupMessages at lines 792–813. Production inbound delivery instead enters apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/channel-persistence-handlers.ts:164, while real allowlist configuration loads through apps/core/src/platform/sender-allowlist.ts:216. Thus this test can pass without proving that configuring only the root sender as allowed prevents another sender's inbound follow-up from producing a turn or reply. Add suite-run coverage through the running runtime's inbound entry point with real allowlist configuration and PostgreSQL, faking only third-party service edges.
findings.title: Not done: answers a thread follow-up only when its sender may trigger the agent

why: Anyone can get a reply in a thread an allowed person started, because the thread check never looks at who sent the new message
